messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 

The test method `testToClass_object()` is calling `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[] array)` with an array containing a non-null string, a null element, and a Double object: `new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d }`. The expected output array of classes is `new Class[] { String.class, null, Double.class }` which means for any input element that is null, the corresponding output class entry should also be null.

Inspecting the source code of `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[] array)`, we see the following flow:
- If the input array is null, it returns null.
- If the input array is empty, it returns an empty Class<?> array.
- Otherwise, it creates a new Class<?> array of the same length.
- Then, it iterates over the input array and for each element `array[i]`, assigns `classes[i] = array[i].getClass()`.

The problem arises in the loop: when `array[i]` is null, calling `array[i].getClass()` triggers a NullPointerException (NPE).

The current bug report's summary and description "c0.m0(Object[]) throws NPE on null array element" exactly matches this diagnosis: the method throws NPE when the array contains null elements.

The failing test confirms this because the input array contains a null element at the second position.

The root cause is a lack of null-check before calling `getClass()` on array elements.

No recent bug reports are relevant to this issue.

Thus, the bug occurred because `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[] array)` does not handle null elements in the input array safely and calls `getClass()` on a null reference leading to the NPE.

Suggested fix would be to check for null elements in the loop and assign null to the output in that case instead of invoking `getClass()`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
